FOREWORD 1-his Indian Standard (Part 1) was adopted by Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Gas Cylinders Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Divisio~ Council. Acetylene gas is distributed to consumers from a source such as a generation plant or cylinder discharge man ifold by means of pipelines. [n view of the explosive behaviour of acebjlene in piping systems, special precautions need to be taken in design, fabrication, erection, testing and commissioning of acetylene gas pipelines. This Code stipulates engineering requirements for safe design, construction and commissioning of acetylene gas pipelines. It is based on the concept of `Working Ranges', which also has been followed by Industrial Gases Committee (lGC) Paris. The concept of' Working Range' includes a combination of parameters, `Detonation Pressure Limit', nature and place of ignition. such as `I)eflagration Pressure Limit',

`['heguidelines given in this code are based on published information and observations made by various authorities on the subject of acetylene gas in pipelines. It is expected that adherence to the guidelines presented in this Code will significantly reduce the safety hazard related to acetylene transmission through pipeline systems. Behaviour of acetylene gas transmitted in pipelines is given in Annex C. This Code is being published Part 2 For pressures Unless otherwise in two parts. Part 2 is as under:

from 155 kPa (g) to 2550 kPa (g). in this Code are gauge pressures.

This Code is intended to recommend safety requirements for design and construction of acetylene pipelines having a working pressure 155 kPa (g) (1.55 kg/cm2 g) but less than 2550 kPa (g) (26 kg/cm2 g). This covers pipelines connecting acetylene compressors and high pressure dryers as well as filling and discharge manifolds for acetylene. Unless otherwise stated, the pressures mentioned in this Code are gauge pressure. In the preparation a) b) c) of this code, assistance has been derived from the following publications:

Code of practice for acetylene pipelines based upon working ranges (IGC Document No. 9/78/E). Acetylene transmission for chemical synthesis, recommended minimum Compressed Gas Association (CGA), USA Pamphlet No. G. 1.3. Standards for valves and piping specification of the Committee responsible practices for piping systelm,

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2: 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

ACETYLENE
PART 1 SCOPE 1.1 This code covers the design, fabrication, erection, testing and commissioning of acetylene gas pipelines having a maximum working pressure (PW) of 155 kPa (g) (1.5 kg/cn12 g) operating at a temperature up to 60�C. The pipeline covered herein is intended to convey commercially available gaseous acetylene containing small amounts of impurities normally present when produced from calcium carbide as per IS 1040 and used for welding, brazing, cutting and allied process. 1.2 Conveying pipe size covered under this Code is up to and including a nominal diameter DN 100 mm. However, it is generally recommended to restrict the pipe size to DN 50. Pipes of size up to DN 100 maybe used only wherever special requirement calls for their use. 1.3 This code does not cover the following: a) b) Pipelines conveying mixtures of acetylene gas with dilutents, Pipelines for interconnecting acetylene compressor with downstream equipment such as dryers and acetylene gas cylinder filling manifolds, Cylinder discharge manifolds, and Acetylene pipelines in a chemical plant where the gas is used as a process feed material. this code is prepared in

PIPELINES -- CODE OF PRACTICE
1 FOR PRESSURES UP TO 155 kPa (g) 3 TERMINOLOGY 3.1 Deflagration A flame produced by decomposition or combustion that travels into the unreacted gas at a velocity which is less than that of sound. The rate of propagation of a deflagration flame increases with the density, the temperature and the turbulence of unreacted gas. Since these three parameters tend to increase as a deflagration progresses, the rate of propagation is usually not steady but tends to increase continuously and sometimes lead to detonation. 3.2 Detonation A flame produced by decomposition or combustion that travels into the unreacted gas, a rate above the speed of sound. Unlike a deflagration, where the pressure ahead or behind the flame front rises at the same time, a detonation involves a sharp difference in pressure between the reacted and unreacted gas. The change from the low pressure of the unreacted gas to the high pressure of the reacted gas takes place in a shock wave at the front of the flame. 3.3 Flame or Flash Back Arrestor An equipment, which quenches a flame front (flashback or decomposition). It shall be suitable for flame, which may occur due to de flagration andlor detonation. Its design and application shall be such that it shall withstand and be effective in stopping a flame coming from either one or both directions (see also IS 11006). 3.4 Manifolds A system in which two or more individually valved, dissolved acetylene cylinders are connected by pipes or hoses to a common inlet header through which al I cylinders are charged simultaneously without dismantling the cylinders or are normally discharged simultaneously through the common outlet header. 3.5 Nominal Diameter (DN)

4.3.2.1 The main acetylene header of Class 2 and Class 3 category shall be run not closer than fifteen metres from any buildings, tire protection facilities Iike water reservoirs and pump houses and storage tank facilities containing hazardous flammable liquids and fuel gas storage facilities like gas holder, etc. In case of locations where possibility of fire and explosion hazards exist, provision of increased safety distances beyond fifteen metres shall be made. Extreme caution shall be exercised in routing acetylene gas pipelines near tunnels, buildings and sewers to avoid the possibility of leaking acetylene gas in such installations. 4.3.2.2 Pipeline route shall be away from location of heat sources like burners, open flames, pilot lamps, welding torches, heating elements, boilers, incinerators, burning or glowing materials/metals, cinders, etc. 4.3.2.3 Location and travel path of moving machines shall be identified and the acetylene gas pipeline shal I be routed such that they are avoided. Places of occurrences of vibration wherever heavy equipment movement or handling of heavy materials are involved shall be avoided while routing the acetylene gas pipelines. 4.3.2.4 Electrical cable(s) shall not be routed along with acetylene gas pipe work. 4.3.2.5 Installation of acetylene gas pipelines in pipe racks carrying other service pipelines which may require maintenance of a type in which either high temperature or heavy equipment is employed, is not allowed. Routing of high operating temperature pipelines, fuel gas or liquid fuel, steam and oxygen pipelines shall also be avoided along with acetylene gas pipelines, as far as possible. 4.3.2.6 All overhead yard acetylene gas pipelines shall be routed such that they have a minimum clearance of 6 metres between bottom of supporting structures and top of road crown/ railway tracks. The pipelines laid over tracks carrying hot materials shall have a minimum clearance often metres and shall be provided with heat shields of suitable design. 4.3.2.7 Underground or buried acetylene gas pipel ines shall be laid with a minimum earth covering of 1.2 In in areas subject to temporary loads. Acetylene gas pipelines shall not be laid underground wherever permanent load like buildings including its aprons, equipment foundation, etc, is built. In case of underground road crossings, pipelines shall be used and in such case minimum distance for entrance and exit from edge of crossings, depth of fill over pipe 3

4.3 Layout 4.3.1 Acetylene pipework shall preferably be routed overhead. However, underground routing may also be permitted, if the requirement so demands.

IS 15190 (Part 1) :2002 sleeves, location of sleeve vent and type of seal for sleeve shall be included in the design. 4.3.2.8 The bleeder pipes from purging connections and relief valve outlets of acetylene lines shall be routed upward and terminated at a height of at least two metres above building roof, or other structures such as pipe racks, to prevent exposure of people to the vent outlets. 4.3.2.9 Acetylene pipeline shall not be used for supporting any other pipelines or electrical cable trays/ racks/individual cables. 4.4 Platforms access ladders, hand railings, etc, shall be provided to facilitate access to instruments and accessories. For easy operation and maintenance of valves, instruments and accessories shall be located above two metres from ground level. 4.5 All acetylene pipes and flanges shall be electrically bonded and grounded properly. At flanged and bolted connections jumpers or shake proof washers (see IS 5371) may be installed for continuity of grounding 4.6 Insulation All overhead acetylene gas pipelines shall be protected against excessive external heat and possible formation of liquid acetylene. The pipelines may be insulated to achieve this. In all cases of insulation provided on acetylene lines, claddings (vapour barriers) shall be of fire resistant type. b) 4.7 Pipe Sizing The diameter of a pipeline shall be finalized so that the required pressure is available at consumer, with the maximum flow in a given pipe run. It is recommended that the velocities be maintained between two to four metres per second for sizing of pipelines. Generally if calculated pipe size becomes more than DN 50 then multiple pipes of DN 50 and smaller diameter may be used to meet the required flow rate. 4.8 Expansion and Flexibility c) d) 3) 4.8.3 The provision for expansion and flexibility shal I take into consideration the maximum possible temperature differential between the design temperature and the ambient temperature in cold season. 4.9 Valves and Measuring Devices

4.9.1 Valves shall be provided on acetylene gas pipework for isolation of pipe sections and equipment, control of pressure and flow, venting, drain iilg, pressure relief, etc. They shall be suitable for service conditions in all respects and material as given in 6 and located suitably considering ease of commissioning, decommissioning, operation and maintenance. 4.9.2 The valves provided shall include but not Iim ited to the following: a) Stop valves shall be provided as follows: 1) 2) On all pipelines consumers, both at sources and

In the branch pipes to each consumer both at the point of branching and at entry to each consumerlshop, On long straight pipework without branch lines, at an interval of 400 to 500 m, for sectionalizing, For purging of acetylene pipelines for draining of test fluid/condensate, For pressure gauges. and and

4) 5)

Isolating and bypass valves for flowmeters, filters, etc. Non return valves on all pipelines unidirectional flow. Pressure isolation reducing requiring

regulating valves together with and relief valves for all pressure installations.

e)

Manual drain valves at low points and manual vent valves at all high points of pipe work.

4.10 Drains Provisions shall be made to drain accumulated condensate or testing fluid from acetylene pipelines. To ensure condensate drainage and liquid drainage. pipelines shall be laid with a gradient of about I nlm/ m run towards the drainage points. Drainage points shall be provided at the lowest points of acetylene gas pipe work and special provisions shall be made in its design to prevent entry of air into the acetylene line and to prevent freezing of any seal liquid used. The size of the drain pipelines shall be such that the entire pipeline between sectionalizing valves can be drained within the desired time period, which shall be not more than 30 min. 4

4.8.1 All acetylene gas pipelines shall be anchored at suitable intervals. The pipelines shall be designed to provide sufficient flexibility to prevent development of undesirable forces or moments at points of connection to equipment, at anchorage or at guide points due to thermal expansion/contraction. 4.8.2 Flexibility shall be provided by changes of direction or by the use of bends, loops or offsets. Wherever no self-compensation can be used to cater for the expansion deformation of the pipelines, expansion loops (U-loops) shall be used. Expansion bellows shall not be used on acetylene pipelines.

IS 15190 (Part 1) :2002 4.11 Purging Facilities 4.12.1.2 The following locations shall be instal led with flashback arrestors at: a) the outlet of the source of acetylene gas such as a generation plant or discharge manifo Id rack; the entrance and exit of gasholders, if installed, within the acetylene gas conveying systenls; the exit of each booster, if any installed the acetylene gas pipeline; on

4.11.1 It is recommended that provisions be made for purging all section(s) of acetylene conveying pipelines with nitrogen gas. Purge systems shall be protected against backflow of acetylene from acetylene lires into the purging medium pipes. In the design of the acetylene lines there should be no dead end sections, which cannot be positively purged. The purging bleeders of acetylene pipelines shall not be combined with the purging bleeder of any other pipeline. All purge connections shall be so designed that pulling of air into the acetylene system is not possible and shall be so located as to prevent accumulation of condensate. One purging bleeder installed in one section of the acetylene gas pipeline shall be not combined with the bleeder of any other section of the same pipeline. If temporary purging connections are to be provided, the design shall be such that it should prevent accidental connection of any system other than the purge gas. Sampling points shall be provided with proper valving for collection of acetylene gas required for analyzing its composition while charging. All purging connections from nitrogen line to acetylene preferably shall be made with flexible hose, so that they can be disconnected on completion of purging, 4.11.2 Since acetylene gas pipelines will be subjected to hydraulic test according to 10.2.7, it shall be provided with vent points with valves at high points and led upward as given in 4.3.2.8. 4.11.3 All such outlet points of venting and purging shall be installed in such a way as to have the possibility for purging and venting of all pockets in the acetylene gas pipelines. 4.12 Safety Devices Safety devices are installed in acetylene gas pipelines to provide protection from hazardous condition that may result due to exceeding of permitted maximum pressure, the propagation of acetylene decomposition, the entry of air or oxygen or flashback. The classification of acetylene pipelines into one of the three classes as prescribed in this code may in some cases call for special requirements of safety devices. Therefore, while making selection of safety devices or in finalizing the set parameters of safety devices, consideration shall be given to the limit of class of pipelines. 4.12.1 Flashback Arrestors

4.12.1.3 The location of flashback arrestors shall be selected depending upon the type, size and class of pipelines. Flashback arrestors shall be provided for separation of sections which fall into different class categories (see Notes under Table 1). 4.12.1.4 In an acetylene gas distribution network of Class 3 category where one or more ring mains are formed by joining one or more points in the pipeline system, each ring main shall be protected by a flash back arrestor unless the pipeline is designed in accordance with 5.3.2.2 and 5.3.2.3. 4.12.1.5 When a single unit of flashback arrestor is not adequate to handle required flow rate; multiple units of flashback arrestor shall be installed for parallel operation. And the individual gas inlets, outlets and liquid drain connections shall be interconnected to respective common headers. 4.12.2 Safety Relief Valves 4.12.2.1 A safety relief valve shall be set so as to open and relieve the gas when the pressure in the pipework being protected by it exceeds 1.1 times the maximum working pressure. The safety relief valve shal I be capable of a flow rate equal to or greater than the maximum flow in the pipeline. 4.12.2.2 Safety relief valves of reliable design and performance, which are able to keep pressure within 10 percent above the maximum working pressure, shall be selected. Material of construction shal I be according to 6. 4.12.2.3 No isolation valve should be provided at the safety valve line. 4.13 Supports for Overhead Pipework

4.13.3 Supports for overhead pipework within shops may be taken from shop structures, columns, trusses, etc, wherever suitable shop structures are not available, pipes shall be supported on trestles, towers and/or pipe bridges. 4.13.4 All supporting elements, except for springs shall be designed for the weight of the pipe filled with water and the weight of insulation, if any. Thrust load shall be considered wherever significant, Other loads such as thermal and frictional load, weight of fittings, condensate, internal pressures, wind load, etc, shall be considered wherever applicable. 4.13.5 Anchors or restraints shall be provided to secure the desired points of piping in fixed positions, They shall permit the line to expand and contract freely in opposite directions away from the anchored point and shall be so arranged as to be structurally suitable for the particular location, line and loading conditions under consideration. 4.13.6 For insulated pipes, if any, steel protectors for the insulation shall be provided at points where the pipe is supported on rollers, slides or other elements requiring contact outside the insulation. 4.13.7 The maximum unsupported shall be as given in Table 3. span for pipelines

5.3 Pipes for Class 3 Category 5.3.1 Pipes falling in Class 3 category shall be designed to withstand decomposition of acetylene gas occurring due to detonation. Class 3 category of pipelines are those where initiation and/or development of detonation is possible. The shockwave traveling along acetylene gas pipeline, as a result of the occurrence of detonation will create conditions of high stress, wherever the same is reflected, like in locations where sharp bends, valves and blanked or dead are installed. 5.3.2 Class 3 category pipes considering the following: a) b) shall be designed

5.3.2.3 At all locations of reflection points as per category 5.3.2(b), for example, blanked ends, valves and bends (of radius less than 5 times the internal diameter (d), tee joints, etc, the increased thickness shall not be less than twice that of the wall thickness and in accordance with equation (4) as applicable. This reinforcing thickness must be selected for a length of pipe of at least three times the internal diameter. 5.4 Wherever a reflection point is protected by a flashback arrestor which is located within predetonation distances from the reflection point, provision of increased wall thickness is not necessary. 5.5 Smooth pipe bends (excluding meter bends) having bend radius of 5 times the internal diameter (d) or more may be considered as straight sections, where the fabrication/manufacture of the bend does not make it weak compared to straight pipes. 5.6 It must be ensured that there is no sudden change in the internal dimensions or shape particularly while designing the reinforcements at reflection points. 5.7 The minimum thickness tm calculated in accordance with Equations (1), (2), (3) and (4) do not include mechanical, corrosion and erosion allowances. 6.1 Steel is recommended as the main material of construction for acetylene transmission systems. In a pipeline system, materials for all components like joints, seals, gaskets, diaphragms, hoses, etc, shall be so chosen that they are adequately resistant to the action of commercial grade acetylene, including its impurities as indicated in IS 1040 and 1S308 and solvents like acetone (if present) under the system operating conditions (that is tempei-ature/pressure) and resistant to atmospheric corrosion. 6.2 Selection of materials shall be made for a pipel ine system so that it is capable to withstand the stresses at the maximum operating pressure. Special consideration shall also be given to thermal and mechanical stresses occurring for pipelines designed to operate under Class 2 and Class 3 category. 6.2.1 The tensile strength of carbon steels used for the construction of acetylene gas pipelines of Class 2 and Class 3 category shall not be less than 320 MPa and elongation atler fracture shall be greater than or equal to 8 400 divided by the minimum tensile strength, but not less than 17 percent in any case. For these categories of pipelines, materials susceptible to aging or brittle fractures shall not be used. 6.2.2 Acetylene pipelines andlor its components may explode when subjected to friction or shock, or if, it contains copper, silver and mercury which forms compounds with acetylene even when present in small quantities under certain operating conditions. Presence of aluminum, magnesium and zinc results in severe corrosion when they come in contact with impure acetylene. The presence of the above metals shal I be avoided. In view of the above copper and copper bearing metal containing copper more than 70 percent shall not be 7

5.8 The equations (2), (3) and (4) shall apply to seam less pipes. For welded pipes according to 7.1, a

IS 15190 (Part 1) :2002 used for acetylene service. For the construction of filters or sieves in which case large surfaces come in contact with unpurified acetylene, special consideration shall be made. In case of use of silver alloys for the purpose of brazing, silver and copper content shall be less than 43 percent and 21 percent respectively. The gap between two parts to be brazed shall be less than 0,33 mm. Special care must be taken to minimize area of filler metal exposed to acetylene and to remove as far as practical all traces of flux. 6.3 Sight glasses, U-tube manometers and similar devises shall be so designed that they are protected against external damage or made to withstand breakage or shall be used in such applications where their breakage shall not cause hazardous conditions. The glasses used for the applications shall be of toughened class and protected with external cover [see 1S 2553 (Part 1); IS 5428 (Part 1); IS 5428 (Part 2) and IS 5428 (Part 4)]. 6.4 For the manufacture of fittings, valve bodies or similar components, ferrous alloys (see IS 1030, 1S 2856 and IS 7899) are suitable for use in pipeline Class 3 category. Spheroidal graphite cast iron (see IS 1865) and wrought iron are also suitable for use in pipeline Class 2 category. Apart from the above ferrous metals, malleable iron (see IS 14329) may also be permitted for use in pipeline Class 1 category, under special cases. 7 COMPONENTS 7.1 Pipes Pipes for acetylene service shall be seamless. Electric resistance welded (ERW) pipes with a guaranteed weld joint efficiency may be used. Hot finished welded (HFW) pipes as per IS 1239 (Part 1) shall not be used. 7.3.2.2 For Class 1 category pipelines, fittings Iike tees and reducers fabricated from pipes may be used. All bends shall be smooth bends. They maybe either cold bends (for pipes DN 50 and below) or hot bends. Bends radius shall not be less than 1.5 times DN. Forged reducer may be used or they maybe made from

1S 15190 (Part 1) :2002 pipes by taper cutting and welding. The design of fittings shall be such that after fabrication their minimum thickness remains equal to or greater than that for straight pipes. 7.3.2.3 For Class 2 and Class 3 category pipelines bends, tees and reducers shall be forged carbon steel. The design of fittings shall be as specified in 5.2 and 5.3 to withstand the deflagration and denotation conditions respectively. Bends may be either hot bends or forged bends, Radius of bends shall preferably be 5 times the nominal diameter of pipe but in no case is less than 1.5 times the nominal diameter of the pipe on which they are used. 7.3.2.4 Reducers for Class 2 and Class 3 category pipelines shall have maximum size reduction of two sizes per reducer. For example reducers of size 50 x 40 mm and 50 x 25 mm maybe used but sizes of 50 x 20 mm shall not be used. 7.3.2.5 Tees shall be right-angled tees shall be avoided. type. 7.8 Regulators Regulators used for pipeline in Class 2 and Class 3 categoty shall either be protected from decomposition or shall be designed to withstand such decomposition without bursting the body. It shall be ensured that the membrane and seal materials comply with requirements specified in 6. 7.9 Hoses 7.9.1 Hoses shall be used where rigid pipes are not suitable. The length of the hoses shall be as minimum as possible. 7.9.2 Tbe thickness for hoses used in Class 1 category shall withstand 1.5 times the maximum working pressure. 7.9.3 Hoses for pipelines of Class 2 category shall have a bursting pressure of not less than 11 times the maximum absolute working pressure. 7.9.4 Hoses for pipelines of Class 3 category shall have a bursting pressure of not less than 35 times the maximum absolute working pressure. 7.9.5 Special considerations should be given to the design of the end fittings for hoses, particularly to avoid sudden changes in internal diameter. Wherever a change in diameter is required, a gradual taper should be made. 7.9.6 Where hoses are used in an installation it must be ensured that for protection of electrostatic charging the resistance between two end couplings, shall not exceed 10c ohms. 7.3.2.6 Use of mitered bends is not allowed for any classes of pipelines. 7.4 Gaskets -- Compressed asbestos gaskets to [S 2712, Grade W/3 of at least 1.6 mm thickness is recommended for use in acetylene service. 7.5 Nuts and Bolts For Class 1 category pipelines nuts and bolts conforming to 1S 1367 (Part 1 to Part 3) shall be used. For Class 2 and Class 3 category pipelines high tensile alloy steel bolts/studs and nuts according to IS 3757and IS 6623 shall be used. 7.6 Flashback Arrestors -- Flashback arrestor installed on acetylene gas pipeline shall conform to 1S 11006. 7.7 Pressure Gauges 7.7.1 Class 1 category pipelines shall be fitted with any type of pressure gauges suitable for acetylene gas at the working pressure. 7.7.2 Pressure gauges for Class 2 and 3 category pipelines shall comply with one of the following: a) The pressure gauge withstands the pressures resulting from acetylene decomposition without serious leakage, A properly sized vent closed with a bursting disc shall be provided for allowing the escape of gas in a safe direction away from the working area. b)

8.1 All steel pipework shall be of socketibutt welded construction. Uses of socket weld joints are however, preferred. Welds on pipelines shall be located at places where the minimum bending stresses occur as far practicable. Flanges shall be provided on straight lengths as required for easy erection and maintenance. Flanged joints shall also be provided to match the connecting ends of equipment, valves and fittings, etc. Where screwed connections are permitted, the same may be provided of acceptable standard (see IS 554). Number of flanged and/or screwed joints shall be

1S 15190 (Part 1) :2002 restricted to a minimum of gas leakage. to minimize the possibility 8.4.2 Smooth bends shall normally 5 times the nominal diameter. 8.4.3 Standard bends and elbows as per relevant IS 1239 (Part 2) the service. Bends and elbows welding ends unless otherwise have a radius of

8.2 Joints are recommended to be assembled with the inside of aIl pipes and fittings smooth, clean and free from burrs, blisters, scale, welding slag, sand and dirt, etc. The inside edges of pipes and turnings shalI be reamed after cutting to remover burrs. Wherever possible the inside of the weld without backing rings shall be ground smooth. Flange faces shall be flee from particles of weld metal. 8.3 Welding 8.3.1 All jointing by electric arc and gas welding process shall be according to IS 816 and IS 1323 respectively. However, provisions of statutory regulations and fire protection manual of the Insurance Association of India, shall be complied with, wherever applicable. 8.3.2 All welding work shall be carried out by qualified welders. All filler materials, edge preparation, post-weld treatment shall give a good welding. All welds shall be made in such a manner that complete fusion and penetration are obtained without an excessive amount of filler metal beyond the root areas. Reinforcements, wherever required shall be applied in such a manner that it will have a smooth pipe and welded fittings. 8.3.3 Pipe and attachments shall be aligned accurately and held firmly prior to welding. If tack welds are used, the tacks shall be either fused into the first layer of weld or else chipped out. All welds shall be built up by the application of multiple beads or passes; the thickness of metal deposited in each bead or pass shall not exceed 3 mm. Each bead shall be cleaned and, if not a work hardening material, shall be lightly penned before the next bead is laid. The complete weld and surrounding pipe shall be cleaned of slag and metal splatter on all surfaces and the inside beads shall be ground smooth where practicable. 8.3.4 Welded carbon steel piping need not be stressrelieved except where specified. 8.3.5 Fabrication of bends by cutting and welding of pipe is not allowed. Branches, reducers, etc, may be fabricated fi-om pipes, by cutting and welding as above, wherever permitted by this code, 8.4 Bending -- Metallic Pipework

SECTION 4 ERECTION, INSPECTION AND TESTING 9 ERECTION 9.1 General 9.1.1 All pipework shall be erected in conformity these code requirements. 9.1.2 Pipes shall be cut to measurement without forcing or springing except springing is explicitly specified. 9.1.3 Unions flanges shall equipment, dismantling such unions minimum. with

and installed where cold

wherever permitted by this code, or be installed in all piping connections to valves, instruments, etc, to facilitate for maintenance. However, number of andlor flanges shall be restricted to a

9.2 Buried Pipework 9.2.1 All buried pipework shall be laid with earth cover sufficient to avoid damage from pressure of vibration caused by surface traffic. Minimum earth covering over the pipe shall be 1200 mm from the finished ground level in areas subject to temporary loads. 9.2.2 Large stones, rubble, etc, found during excavation shall be dumped faraway to avoid damage to pipework during backfilling. The trench bottom shall be levelled to the required levels keeping in view the pipe slopes required. In steeply sloping trenches, pipe anchors will be provided. 9.2.3 All buried steel pipework including accessories shall be externally coated and wrapped to prevent corrosion. The coatings shall be coal tar enamel based with intermediate wrapping of fiberglass tissue and final wrapping with bituminized craft paper. The external coating work shall conform to IS 10221 for both material and workmanship. After completion of coating and wrapping, the entire length of the coated pipe shall be tested for defects and defective portions, if any shall be rectified. 9.2.4 For long lengths of underground pipelines through corrosive soil, cathodic protection of the pipeline is recommended. The type and degree of protection shall depend upon the survey of soil resistivity along the proposed pipe route. However, cathodic protection based on the principle of sacrificial

8.4.1 Pipe bends shall be true to angle and have a smooth surface free of flat spots and corrugations. Actual inside diameter at any portion of the pipe shall not deviate by more than +3 percent from the inside pipe diameter.

10

IS 15190 &art 1) :2002 anodes (with minimum life of not less than ten years) is preferred for acetylene pipelines. 9.3 Pipework Installation shall be provided. 9.5 Suitable anchors of concrete shall be provided at bends and other locations in a pipeline where unbalanced pressures may develop under normal or test pressure and tend to cause movement in the pipelines. 9.6 Every precaution shall be taken against the floating of the pipe due to water flowing into the trench or from caving, flushing or puddling. In case of such floating, replacement of the pipe shall be made by making wholly good any injury or damage which may result. 9.7 Valve Chambers 9.7.1 Valves on an underground pipeline shal I be located in a masonry chamber covered with R.C.C. slabs and manhole with cover. The chamber size shal I enable free movement during maintenance and/or repair work to the valves. Chambers which because of their design or construction could become, in any way, hazardous to human life shall not be permitted. The valve chamber shall be properly vented to prevent accidental accumulation of acetylene gas. 9.7.2 The design shall incorporate sufficient escape provisions for personnel in the event of flooding or other emergency. Due to size or maintenance or replacement of valves may require more than one person at a time, a minimum of two manholes shall be provided. Manholes shall be of suitable size and shall be located on the cover slab in opposite locations. 9.7.3 Hydro insulation of manholes for the total height as required. 9.8 Structural Platforms shall be provided

9.3.1 Precautions shall be taken at all times to prevent damage to the coating and wrapping on the pipe and appurtenances by workmen or trespassers. During laying and at any other time while pipe is exposed, no person shall be permitted to walk on a pipe wearing boots or shoes with nails or other attachments that may injure the coating. Care must be exercised to prevent the dropping of tools, rivets and other materials on, and the dragging of heavy objects over a pipe, and other acts that would damage its coating and wrapping. Pipe handling slings and any block used in handling or storing pipe must be well padded to avoid damage to the pipe coating. 9.3.2 Ends of pipes in the storage yard shall be closed by a head or barrier. The heads or barriers shall not be removed until a pipe is about to be laid. Each day, at the close of work and when laying is not in progress, the open ends of a line shall be similarly protected. If it becomes necessary to backfill a trench before making connections to adjacent piping, the open ends shall be closed by suitable timber bulkheads. 9.3.3 After a pipeline has been laid on skids, it shall be thoroughly cleaned, inspected and any damage to the protective coating satisfactorily repaired while the pipe is suspended above the trench. The pipe shall then be lowered into place and laid to the required line and gradient. 9.3.4 After completion and acceptance of the field test on each major section of an underground pipeline, all testing media shall be removed from the section and all interior surfaces cleaned. All abrasions and other damages to the coating shall then be repaired. 9.4 Road and Track Crossing 9.4.1 All underground pipelines crossing rail tracks or roads where the depth of cover from the bottom of the ties or roadbed to the top of pipe is between 1.2 m and 1.8 m shall be protected. This protection shall be by reinforced concrete culvert, reinforced concrete casing pipe, or steel casing pipe or sleeve. The annular space between casing pipe and inner pipe at the ends shall be suitably sealed. Details indicated in 4.3.2.7 shall be followed. 9.4.2 A culvert shall be laid true to line and grade with the bottom quadrant contact with the undisturbed trench bottom with tamping. The culvert shall extend beyond the ends of railroad ties or roadbeds by a distance equal to the depth of bury of the bottom of the pipe. Proper venting of culvert/tunnel/pipe sleeves

and Supports

All reqvired operating platforms, valve stands, access ladders, handrails, etc, shall be erected, after the piping has been installed. Structural steelwork shall follow IS 7205. 10 INSPECTION 10.1 Inspection 10.1.1 The components of the pipework shal I be subjected to visual inspection. The pipeline, after completion of erection, shall be inspected for its conformity with the construction drawings prepared according to the stipulations of this code. 10.1.2 All weld joints shall be visually examined during manufacture, fabrication and erection to ensure conformity with the requirements of this code. 10.2 Pressure Tests 10.2.1 11 Prior to acceptance and initial operation, AND TESTS

IS 15190 (Part 1) :2002 installed piping shall be pressure tested to ensure the system's strength and to ensure that it is leakproof. 10.2.2 In the event any repairs or additions made following the pressure test, the affected piping shall be retested. 10.2.3 A piping system shall be tested as a complete unit or in sections. For the connecting piping and other appurtenances for testing, it is not required that the tie in sections of pipes be pressure tested. 10.2.4 Special components, which require special testing, may be tested separately and/or as per separate test procedure. Test at pressures stipulated in 7.2 shall be performed for valves before installation in addition to testing after installation in the piping system. 10.2.5 Test Medium Testing may be carried out with an inert gas or air, provided sufficient precautions are taken to avoid any risks associated with the tests. 10.2.6 Test Preparation 10.2.6.1 Wherever possible, pipe joints including welds shall be left uncoated and exposed for examination during test. 10.2.6.2 Equipment which is not to be included in the test shall either be disconnected from the piping or isolated by blank flanges. 10.2.6.3 If a pressure is to be maintained for a period of time and the test medium in the system is subject to thermal expansion, precaution shalI be taken to avoid development of excessive pressure, 10.2.6.4 Prior to testing, the interior of the piping system shall be clear of all foreign material. 10.2.7 Hydraulic Test pressure. Observing the pressure over a specified time as given in 10.2.9 can check leak-tightness. Leakage can be detected by means of a soap bubble test. 10.2.8.2 While subjected to test pressure the piping system shall be visually examined for signs of leakage or other defects. Any reduction in test pressure as indicated by pressure gauges shall be deemed to indicate the presence of a leak unless such reduction can be readily attributed to some other cause. 10.2.8.3 If leakage or other defects appear, the affected portion of the piping system shall be repaired or replaced and retested. 10.2.9 Test Duration Test duration shall be not less than 30 min for each 14 m3 of pipe volume or fraction thereof. For piping system having a volume of more than 68 ml, the duration of the test shall not be less than 24 h. 10.2.10 Test Records 10.2.10.1 stipulated 10.2.10.2 All manufacturer's test certificates in 10.1 shall be preserved. as

Records of testing carried out as per and 10.2.8 for each pipe installation shall be made and preserved.

The identification markings must be repeated at regular intervals and visible Iocat ions to ensure that the pipeline/s can be clearly identified and are not confised with adjacent pipelines carrying other substances. Devices against entry of air and oxygen (that is condensate drainage system, etc) shall be checked for proper operation and it has to be ensured that they are not blocked. Wet type flashback arrestors shall also be checked, particularly for maintenance of correct water level. Filters and dry type flashback arrestors shall be examined for proper condition and it has to be ensured that they are not blocked. 12.2.10 The settirfg of pressure regulation/reducing stations shall be as per specified parameter/duty conditions. 12.2.11 All valves at service points, isolation, vent, drain points and equipment connections, etc, shall be checked for complete opening and tight shutoff. 12.2.12 Qualified test personnel should be available throughout the purging/commissioning operations in addition to those deployed for commissioning. They should be equipped with necessary testing instruments in good working conditions. 12.3 Cleaning 12.3.1 Acetylene pipelines must also be properly cleaned internally by blowing compressed air or nitrogen gas through pipes. Velocity of blowing shal I be less between 12 to 20 m/see and pressure at the air/ nitrogen inlet shall be 600 kPa (g) to 700 kPa (g) (6 to 7 kg/cm2 g). All vents, drains, service points including flashback arrestors shall be blown by means of blowing medium. 12.3.2 Wet type flashback arrestors shall be blown after draining the water. After blowing operation is over, the flashback arrestor must be refilled with water up to the correct water level. 12.3.3 Dry type flashback arrestors in-situ by blowing compressed air. 12.4 Preparation may be cleaned

12.2.1 The source of acetylene gas (Generation plant or discharge manifold) is ready to be commissioned or already commissioned. 12.2.2 Various valve operating platforms, platform accesses, walkways, staircases and cat ladder access and all work places are cleared of erection debris. No obstructions shall be lying around. 12.2.3 Safety instructions, notices and displays are securely placed in visible and appropriate locations at regular intervals of the pipeline being taken up for commissioning. 12.2.4 Adequate numbers of tire fighting personnel fire fighting equipment and appliances are placed in appropriate locations. 12.2.5 All drawings, manuals, test certificates issued by the manufacturer and statutory authorities are available with the personnel deployed for commissioning: 12.2.6 The personnel deployed for commissioning shall check the conformity of the system taken up for commissioning with all the drawings documents indicated in 12.2.5, and their satisfaction as regards the conformity shall be recorded. 12.2.7 A survey shall be conducted before the commissioning work is taken up, for the following. 12.2.7.1 All consumers of acetylene shall be kept inoperative till such time that the commissioning of the pipeline is over and the system is certified as being ready to be put into service. 12.2.7.2 All sources of heat and fire must be kept away from the acetylene system. Possibility of sparks from locomotives/automotive, chimneys/stacks, static electricity, and short circuits shall be completely eliminated. 12.2.7.3 Location and travel path of moving machines, automobiles shall be identified and restricted in such a way that they do not create hindrance for the commissioning operation and introduce hazardous situations. 12.2.7.4 Possibility and occurrence of vibration and physical shock to the acetylene pipelines shall be eliminated. 12.2.7.5 Unauthorized use of pipeline as electrical conductor or as a support for other items shall not be made. 12.2.7.6 All electrical are identified. 12.2.8 Inspection installations in the proximity

12.4.1 Nitrogen gas shall be used as purging medium. 12.4.2 If the pipeline is long, then commissioning in sections is recommended. IS 15190 (Part 1) :2002 12.4.3 All purging connections shall be connected with suitable hose and hose couplings with nitrogen supply provisions. 12.4.4Complete isolation of the entire distribution system(s)/pipe(s) to be commissioned from connected systemlacetylene gas sourcelconsuming shopl equipment shall be ensured by completely shutting off isolation valves provided for these purposes. In case of sectionalization of pipelines, isolation valve(s) at each end of section(s) shall remain completely shutoff. 12.4.5 All openings like service points shall remain shutoff by closing the isolation valves provided for the purpose. 12.5 Initializing Purging and Commissioning 12.6.2 For purging operations of yard pipelines and shop internal pipework, nitrogen gas of minimum 97.5 percent purity with a velocity of 15 to 20 m/s shall be used. 12.6.3 Introduction of nitrogen gas shall be continued till samples taken at selected ventipurge out points show satisfactory oxygen contents. The acetylene pipeline may be considered free from air if the outgoing nitrogen contains not more than 2.5 percent oxygen. Nitrogen supply shall be terminated and all isolation/ purloinl drainf vent or purge out valves for the pipeline/section under consideration shall be kept completely shutoff under nitrogen pressure. 12.6.4 Once the purging operation for the section is complete, the nitrogen inlet valve at the source end and the vent valve at the other end shall be closed. The section, which has been purged, shal I remain pressurized with nitrogen gas at a pressure of about 100 kPa (g) (1 kg/cm2 g). 12.6.5 The section of pipeline, which follows the section already purged, shall be taken up for purging in case of a sectionalized purging operation. If the pipeline is a short one and need not be sectionalized, the consuming shop(s) connected may be taken up for purging. 12.6.6 For purging of the next section of pipeline, if applicable, nitrogen gas admission as given in 12.6.1 shall be made for the section just after gas pipeline sectionalizing valve, which isolates the already purged section and the next section downstream. A II the sectionalisation valves in this second section shall remain closed. This process shall be repeated unt iI a II sections of the pipeline are purged and pressurized with nitrogen. 12.6.7 Once a particular section of the pipeIine/shop internal pipework is pressurized by filling with nitrogen and the section ahead (except for a terminal section at consuming end) is also pressurized by nitrogen filling, admission of acetylene gas shall be commenced. Acetylene gas, which is already charged in the earlier, section or-pipeline (for example, at~he start of the entire operation, the source like generation plant or discharge manifold, etc), shall be admitted by opening the inlet isolation valve a few turns. The valves for purge out point and/or discharge points shall be opened. Gas samples shall be collected for measuring acetylene gas concentration. The sect ion or pipeline vent/purge out points shall be closed as soon as the acetylene concentration of 10 percent by volume of nitrogen is reached. 12.6.8 In case of a short pipeline, instead of pressurizing sections ofpipelines with nitrogen as is done for longer pipelines, after the supply pipeline is pressurized with nitrogen, the next consuming shop(s) internal header(s) 14

ANNEX C (Foreword)
BEHAVIOUR OF ACETYLENE GAS TRANSMITTED IN PIPELINES

Acetylene can bum in the presence of air from a range of2 to 82 percent. In case of occurrence of a source of ignition of any form in an acetylene pipeline system, decomposition of acetylene gas into its constituents, namely, carbon and hydrogen, can be initiated even in the near absence of air or oxygen. Hence the design of an acetylene conveying system shall include facilities to keep air/oxygen out of acetylene and to prevent acetylene leakage into air. The appearance of a bright flame, rise in temperature and pressure, and soot formation which resembles the explosive conversion of a mixture of fuel gas and oxygen are characteristics of acetylene decomposition. Propagation of acetylene gas decomposition from the ignition source to the rest of the pipeline depends mainly on the working pressure of the pipeline and its size.

The ignition energy required to initiate the decomposition; its velocity and associated pressure rise within the pipeline are mainly dependent on the working pressure and size of the pipeline. If decomposition of acetylene is initiated in a pipeline due to a source of ignition `de flagration' followed by `detonation' may occur. The defsrtition of' deflagration' reflects the conditions under which the acetylene decomposition occurs and proceeds at a moderate velocity (below sonic) and at which associated rise in pressure to a maximum of 11 to 13 times the initial pressure occurs. The transition from `deflagration' to `detonation' occurs under conditions which are also indicated in the definition for `detonation'. Pipeline conveying acetylene shall be designed, constructed, tested and maintained to prevent occurrence of `deflagration' and `detonation' and withstand the same in case of their occurrence.
